en: The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River formed because slightly acidic rainwater slowly dissolved the surrounding limestone rock over millions of years.
Mount Mayon has a perfect cone shape because its highly viscous lava cools quickly and piles up near the vent.
The Tiwi geothermal plant in Albay generates electricity because underground magma heats water into steam to spin turbines.
The Banaue Rice Terraces prevent soil erosion because their flat steps slow down rainwater runoff on the steep mountains.
The southwest monsoon causes heavy rains because it picks up abundant moisture while traveling over the warm West Philippine Sea.
Tubbataha Reef grows continuously because tiny coral polyps extract dissolved calcium from seawater to build hard limestone skeletons.
The Bangui windmills in Ilocos Norte generate clean electricity because strong coastal monsoon winds spin their massive turbine blades.
The Cagayan River frequently overflows because heavy typhoon rains in the Sierra Madre mountains send massive water volumes downstream.
The Philippines experiences frequent volcanic eruptions because the subduction of tectonic plates melts rock into magma beneath the islands.
Lake Taal fills its basin because an ancient volcanic eruption caused the ground to collapse into an empty magma chamber.
The Sierra Madre mountains block moisture-laden monsoon winds, creating a dry rain shadow effect over the central Luzon plains.
Mangrove forests in Panguil Bay protect the coastline because their dense, tangled roots absorb the energy of crashing ocean waves.
